claims.text: Refractory alloying elements and Cu have a high positive heat of mixing.
A mixed RHEA-element/Cu powder precursor naturally tends to segregate because of this positive heat of mixing.
Optimized SPS processing can mitigate the detrimental effects associated with the positive heat of mixing between refractory elements and Cu.
Optimized SPS can produce a homogeneous and stable RHEA-Cu composite microstructure at large scale.
Heating rate, applied pressure, and dwell time are the SPS parameters to be optimized through a data-driven or machine-learning framework.
SPS provides rapid heating and high-pressure, high-temperature sintering conditions.
The proposed SPS conditions mimic conditions relevant to next-generation nuclear-reactor structural components.
SPS causes rapid densification of the RHEA-Cu powder compact.
SPS kinetically suppresses phase segregation in the RHEA-Cu composite.
Fast heating, high pressure, and short dwell time delay the diffusional processes that cause Cu segregation.
Data-driven optimization of SPS parameters can make reaction kinetics more uniform and stabilize the composite microstructure.
Optimized SPS will reduce Cu segregation and improve microstructural homogeneity in the RHEA-Cu composite.
The resulting RHEA-Cu composite will have a stable microstructure.
Improved homogeneity and stability will produce superior high-temperature mechanical properties in the RHEA-Cu composite.
Conventional reactive sintering or melting does not adequately control RHEA-Cu reaction kinetics and therefore causes segregation and microstructural inhomogeneity.
Uncontrolled thermal gradients introduced during scale-up could prevent the hypothesized microstructure from forming.
The optimized SPS parameter window may change significantly with powder morphology or alloy composition.
SPS has shown promise for this application at laboratory scale.
The optimized SPS parameter window for large-scale production and its consistency across alloy compositions remain undetermined.
